The day

  1. 7 am
    Up and breakfast
  2. 7:30 am
    Play at home
    • Hallway bowling Line up empty plastic bottles and roll a soft ball at them.
    • Scarf dancing Wave scarves or dish towels high and low, fast and slow, to music.
  3. 8:50 am
    Get ready to go

    Shoes on, the bag, water and a snack.

  4. 9:10 am
    Drive to Blue Jay Point County Park
  5. 9:30 am
    Blue Jay Point County Park
  6. 11:30 am
    Drive home
  7. 11:50 am
    Play at home
    • Animal walks Bear crawl, frog hop, crab walk and penguin waddle from one side of the room to the other.
  8. 12:15 pm
    Lunch
  9. 12:45 pm
    Wind down

    A couple of books to settle.

  10. 1 pm
    Nap
  11. 2 pm
    Up and a snack
  12. 2:20 pm
    Get ready to go

    Shoes on, the bag and a water bottle.

  13. 2:40 pm
    Drive to Northeast Regional Library
  14. 3 pm
    Northeast Regional Library
  15. 4:15 pm
    Drive home
  16. 4:35 pm
    Play at home
    • Animal yoga Stretch like a cat, sit like a frog, stand like a flamingo, curl up like a sleeping mouse.
    • Blanket fort reading Drape a blanket over two chairs and read in there with a flashlight.
  17. 6:30 pm
    Dinner
  18. 7:15 pm
    Bath, books and bed

    Map · Free

    A walk along the greenway and a playground stop make an easy morning in south Wake.

    • Bring a snack and a water bottle.

  • 🌿 Beech Bluff County Park StoryWalk® 2026 (Self-Led), then Beech Bluff County Park

    Beech Bluff County Park · South Wake · 9:30 am–11 am

    Map · Free · No sign-up needed

    Your child reads a picture book one page at a time along the Beech Bluff StoryWalk, then plays at the park next to it.

    • Let your child read the posted pages out loud to you.
    • Bring a snack for the playground.

  • 🌳 Historic Oak View County Park

    Raleigh · 3 pm–4:30 pm

    Map · Free

    A relaxed afternoon walk with the garden and the animals the park is known for, done well before sunset.

    • Bring a snack and a light layer.
    • Ask your child to spot as many animals as they can.

  • 🌳 Apex Nature Park

    Cary / Apex · 3 pm–4:30 pm

    Map · Free

    Your child can follow the greenway and look for leaves, sticks and signs of animals.

    • Bring a small bag for collecting treasures.
    • Pack a snack for a picnic shelter break.
